Strait of Hormuz Updates: 

There is still a complete lack of clarity on what the status is on negotiating a deal between the U.S. and Iran. The admin says one thing and shortly after Iranian official deny the claims.

This means that the Strait of Hormuz remains essentially closed at around 4% of the normal traffic, with potentially more ships turning off their transponders to avoid being targeted. 

Iran has at times offered to allow some tankers and cargo ships to go through depending on if they are “non hostile”, aligned in some way, or pay a toll. This has been spotty and inconsistent at best. 

There remains a global energy crisis that is slowly becoming a major concern, especially in the pacific region that is heavily reliant on Middle Eastern LNG and oil. 

China, Japan, India, Vietnam, Thailand, Sri Lanka, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand, and the Philippines are taking or will soon take measures to address skyrocketing prices and shortages.

Also at risk is the world’s food production as a significant amount of fertilizer is now out of reach. In addition to around 30% of certain fertilizers taken offline due to Hormuz, China has banned 50%-75% of its own fertilizer exports which could amount to an additional 8% of the world’s supply. 

This will have major knock on inflationary effects as the year goes on as well as contribute to food shortages in certain parts of the world as yields decline. 

In short, the Strait of Hormuz needs to open up otherwise the global economy is in deep trouble. 

#Iran #China #StraitofHormuz #Trade #Trump #IranWar‌

The five-second epistemology of the nerds discovering the bullwhip.
Cascading multiplicative effects from the physical scarcity of oil in global markets. Look at all the big words. Cascading. Multiplicative. Physical scarcity. The nerds found a thesaurus. It’s called a bullwhip. One word. The kitchen said it on Day 3. The purchasing manager cancels the safety stock because the jawboning said productive conversations. The jawboning expires. The purchasing manager re-orders into a market that moved against him. The re-order is larger because the fear is larger. The amplification amplifies. The cascade cascades. The multiplicative multiplies. One word. Bullwhip. The nerds writing a dissertation on the thing the kitchen named in one word.

There will be pain. There is pain. Slovenia is rationing. The Philippines declared a national energy emergency. Shell said Europe faces shortages next month. Hapag-Lloyd can’t rescue its own team. Turkey just dumped $8 billion in gold. The DFL at an all-time high in twenty-six years of data. 24 million barrels per day net deficit bigger than COVID. The pain isn’t coming. The pain moved in. The pain redecorated. The pain changed the locks. The nerds saying there will be pain the way The Economist says could weaken for years. Arriving at the present tense using the future tense. The building is on fire and the nerds say there will be heat.

The kitchen said bullwhip. The kitchen said spring loading. The kitchen said face rip. The kitchen said the jawboning is the thing that makes it worse. Rory Johnston said physical markets rip your face off. The nerds said cascading multiplicative effects. Same thesis. Different word count. Some cascading. Some multiplicative. Some bullwhip. Day 27.
